artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d \geq 3$ be an integer and let $V \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be an algebraic variety of dimension at most $d-1$ and of degree bounded by some constant. For a finite set $P \subset V$ of $n$ points, let
$$D(P) = |\{\, \|p - q\| : p, q \in P,\ p \neq q \,\}|$$
denote the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by $P$.

Establish nontrivial lower bounds on $\min_{P \subset V,\ |P|=n} D(P)$ that improve upon the bounds known for unconstrained point sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$, ideally as a function of $n$, $d$, and the geometry (dimension and degree) of $V$. In particular, identify which classes of varieties $V \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ for $d \geq 3$ force any $n$-point subset to determine many distinct distances, and quantify the resulting lower bounds.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial progress exists for specific classes of varieties. Sharir and Solomon proved that $n$ points on a constant-degree two-dimensional algebraic surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ determine $\Omega(n^{7/9}/\mathrm{polylog}\, n)$ distinct distances, and have related results for points on curves/surfaces in three dimensions. The general problem for arbitrary varieties in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $d \geq 3$ remains open and was deliberately posed in vague form.
